Hazelwood School
Dare to break down the conventions of the everyday and discover something new.
This is a place for the innovative thinkers, the bold explorers, and the curious.
Dare to Be You
Dare to Think Big
We are thrilled to announce the appointment of former England Rugby Captain, Chris Robshaw, as our Sports Consultant.
A former star of SD Legion and Harlequins, Chris will coach pupils weekly across a range of sports, sharing his professional expertise both on the field and in training.
His leadership and experience will be instrumental in helping pupils develop essential skills, while his passion for fitness and wellbeing will ensure that all children benefit from his guidance. Mr Robshaw’s approach will also emphasize mental resilience, teaching students to navigate the highs and lows both in sports and in life.
Chris expressed his enthusiasm: “I’m extremely excited to join Hazelwood. Working with young children at such a formative stage in their education is a unique opportunity to shape their approach to fitness and instil a positive mental attitude. I can’t wait to get started!”
Open Mornings Coming Soon
We caught up with British Ambassador to the United States and former Hazelwood pupil, Sir Christian Turner, to find out more about his new role and his time at Hazelwood.
Read the full interview on our Alumni page.
We're delighted to share our latest Muddy Stilettos and Talk Education reviews.
Read them in full on our Reviews page.
We are proud to announce that Hazelwood is a fully accredited Kindness Ambassador School!
Kindness isn't just something we talk about - it is at the very heart of our daily school life.

pageCache.text:
Preparing for Senior School
At Hazelwood, we pride ourselves in offering a unique journey tailored to the individual, which enables our pupils to thrive at the right choice of senior school and beyond.
Tailored Approach
Pupils benefit from small class sizes and skilled subject teachers, offering each pupil a bespoke approach for their needs. We ensure they are prepared for their choice of senior school destination by providing dynamic and rigorous content across subjects, with adaptable pupil assessment techniques based on pupils’ individual needs through a variety of different methods.
Revision Workshops
Careers Talks
Provided several times a year to give pupils insight into the kinds of future job opportunities that are available. This is further supported by weekly careers-based lessons in form time and key speaker presentations from leading industry experts.
Senior School Success
Online Portfolios
In order to record the range of their achievements throughout Years 7 & 8, pupils create their own online portfolios to store and present their assessments and any other work they and their teachers feel should be celebrated. Pupils can share this online record of their work with prospective senior schools.
CASE
Pupils who wish to sit the Common Academic Scholarship Examination are prepared through support sessions and alternative homework tasks. We have ensured that our curriculum is flexible enough to allow for simultaneous CASE preparation.
Assessments
Other subjects are assessed formally in a variety of ways which allow children to develop a range of skills, such as debating, problem solving, presenting, mind mapping, research and role-play, alongside more traditional writing exercises, such as essays, letters and reports. Using a variety of assessment methods allows children to find different ways of expressing their understanding, while developing confidence in these disciplines.
Confidence Building & Incremental Acceleration
Our curriculum is incrementally accelerated, ensuring that there is a calm and controlled approach to the examination process. This ensures that our pupils possess an inner confidence and intellectual curiosity, which makes them well placed to embrace the challenges of entrance exams.
We offer small classes, with teaching led by experienced, dynamic, secondary trained mathematics teachers, enthusiastic to pass on their love and enjoyment of the subject. Our pupils leave with the skills and understanding required to be one step ahead on the road to their success at GCSE and beyond.
Roma Phillimore Head of Maths
Our Senior School Transition Officer maintains close links with senior schools to ensure that we’re equipping our pupils with the skills and knowledge they require to be ready for their senior school journey.
Open communication between parents and Hazelwood staff is key. Our dedicated staff team know your child and we can help guide pupils towards a selection of schools where we believe your child will thrive as an individual based on a depth of knowledge of both your child and the senior schools.
Hazelwood does a brilliant job of bringing its pupils to 'Senior School Readiness’ as I term it – a curious and independent mind, paired with a stable and strong sense of self; a practical independence and a passion for and commitment to academic learning.
I wanted to write and tell you how pleased we are that we decided to keep our son at Hazelwood for Years 7 and 8 … gave him time to mature and develop before beginning his journey at his senior school. The experiences that he had during his last 2 years in particular were incredible.
A highlight was definitely the Year 8 Leavers Programme - I don't think his senior school will be able to match that! The friendships that he developed during his time at Hazelwood are really strong … Hazelwood helped prepare him really well for his senior school and whilst he left with some sadness, he was really excited about joining his new school. He has settled in really well and had no problem meeting new friends. The curriculum and style of teaching prepared him really well as he starts his GCSE's and I am pleased to say that he appears unfazed by them.
He oozes confidence and takes most things in his stride now … my son is so happy to go to school and seems much happier in himself. I have no doubt that he will excel in whatever he chooses to do as he is beginning to find the determination to succeed inside himself. I thought that you would be interested to hear how things are going, and I also wanted to tell you that all your, and your staff's, hard work has really paid off. My ‘child’ doesn't appreciate it now, but the foundations that you all gave him to build on were fantastic. So again, thank you.
My children’s growth in confidence and also their achievement is down to their and Hazelwood’s combined efforts. They have grown up so much over the last year and have surprised my husband and me by their high levels of determination, self-motivation and achievements. They were very committed to working over the holidays with past assessment papers, but also were able to enjoy life and put things into perspective. We still had time for a holiday, garden cricket and football camp!
Thank you so much for the foundations you gave them. A good grounding in all the subjects, and a good dose of resilience and initiative have stood them in very good stead.
Senior School Destinations
We take great care in preparing each child for a senior school most appropriate for their personality, academic ability and talent. The wide range of senior schools reflects Hazelwood’s broad education and excellent record in securing the right school for every child.
My children have been shaped by their school and I am incredibly proud of the young adults they are. I will always be grateful for the impact an amazing school can have on a child.

Upper School Curriculum
From Year 5 upwards, pupils enjoy being taught by individual subject teachers across all subjects, delivering increased variety, independence and opportunity throughout their learning.
We offer specialist English and Maths teaching and tailored homework to prepare pupils for a variety of different senior school tests. We use online software to prepare pupils for their ISEB pre-tests.
Academic Rigour
Staff take pride in their own subjects and carefully differentiate all lessons to support and stretch pupils according to their needs. We are accredited by NACE (National Association for Able Children in Education) for the quality of our differentiation and provision for stretching pupils.
Comprehensive Learning & Support
Despite being a non-selective school, all year groups at Hazelwood are working ahead of expectations for their age in English, Maths and Science and we have impressive predictors of GCSE success based on the MidYIS assessments completed in Year 7.
Our Learning Support Department is also on hand to monitor any emerging needs or difficulties pupils might have in their learning.
Rich Opportunities
Our academic rigour is the foundation and fuel for children to become creative with their learning. Beyond core lessons, their Humanities, Science, DT, Games, Creative Arts, Performing Arts and BOX lessons give pupils the opportunity to develop skills across a range of disciplines and apply their learning in different, creative ways to develop them into deep thinkers, questioners, analysers and problem solvers.
Future-Ready Individuals
We provide pupils with an exceptional education which enables them to flourish, grow and mature into future-ready, confident individuals:
We’ve experienced first-hand how each of our children is stretched academically, according to their own ability and according to their secondary school aspirations.
I achieved two 9’s in my English GCSEs and don’t think I would have achieved this without all your help and support whilst I was at Hazelwood. Thank you very much.

Awards and Inspections
From prestigious industry awards to rigorous inspections, our dedication to providing exceptional education is consistently acknowledged and celebrated.
Commended - Independent Prep School of the Year 2026
Hazelwood has been awarded 'Commended' for Independent Prep School of the Year by the Independent School of the Year Awards 2026.
We are delighted to have been recognised for this award and we are so thankful to our pupils, staff and families who make our community so special.
Talk Education Awards 2024 - Innovation in Education
Hazelwood is a proud finalist in the 2024 Talk Education Awards Innovation in Education.
This nomination reflects Hazelwood's continued efforts to provide a bold and innovative approach to learning, equipping pupils with the skills needs for today's changing world.
Muddy's Best Schools Awards 2024
Hazelwood is a proud finalist in the 2024 Muddy Stilettos Best Schools Awards for Best Experiential Learning.
This accolade recognises Hazelwood's continued whole-school ethos on innovative and adaptive approaches, focusing on personalised learning journeys for all pupils.
Chartered College of Teaching Member Status
Hazelwood School has been granted Institutional Member Status by the Chartered College of Teaching, the professional body for teachers. This designation recognises our commitment to professional learning, evidence‑informed practice, and supporting our staff’s development. Through this partnership:
iExcellence Award
As an i25 Joint Finalist in the iExcellence awards 2020, we were delighted to have our spirit of invention recognised for our innovative suite – the inside and outside BOX.
The BOX is our flexible, agile-learning space which inspires and aids dynamic teaching and learning. A space which is unlike a traditional classroom, there are no set rules, instead it heralds an inclusive new way of learning that is full of investigative possibility.
The iExcellence Award recognises influencers and innovators in the independent education sector who have made a real impact.
Hazelwood is passionate about embracing digital literacy of the future.
My daughter has had an invaluable opportunity to broaden her horizons and is really excited about the future and what it holds for her generation.
The BOX creates an environment where pupils take risks and approach tasks from a new angle. They feel safe making mistakes. The collaboration and creativity the children exhibit while working in the BOX has transferred to the classroom, where they are taking ownership of their thinking and learning.
Teacher at Hazelwood.
ISI Report – June 2023
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) is responsible for the inspection of schools with a membership to an Independent Schools Council association.
The report is a detailed assessment of the School, examining provision, curriculum, teaching, pastoral care, governance, leadership and culture.
Happy, Confident Children
We are proud to have passed our latest inspection report in June 2023 again as we are always striving to make improvements and identify where we can better enhance our pupils’ education. The report reflects the ongoing work we are doing to provide a motivating environment at Hazelwood for happy, confident children and to ensure they are well prepared and ready for the next stage of their education.

Bursaries
Financial Assistance
At Hazelwood, we strongly believe in creating a diverse and inclusive pupil body, irrespective of financial backgrounds. We are committed to breaking down barriers to access by ensuring pupils with potential, talent and ambition are not hindered by financial constraints.
Offering pupil bursaries can have a transformative impact on the lives of pupils and their families by influencing their academic achievements, personal development and future opportunities. This leads to a more equitable and enriched learning environment for the entire School community.
Each year, we support children and families through a range of means-tested financial awards (bursaries), which are managed through a third-party supplier. This enables some children to attend Hazelwood by providing financial assistance with fees and other costs.
If you would like to talk to us about applying for financial assistance for a place for your child, please contact the Admissions Department on 01883 912037 or [email protected]
All applications for assistance are treated in the utmost confidence.
The Gift of Opportunity
By supporting Hazelwood School’s Bursary Fund, you can help give talented and deserving children the opportunity to benefit from an exceptional education—regardless of their financial circumstances. Your gift, no matter the size, can make a lasting difference in a child’s life and help us continue our commitment to inclusivity, excellence, and opportunity for all.

Fees
Explore our fee structure and payment options from nursery to Year 8.
Upper & Lower School Fees
The government announced that effective from 1 January 2025, VAT at a rate of 20% would be applied to Independent School fees.
We have taken proactive measures to manage the additional charge in a way that reduces the impact on our families. Effective from January 2025, Hazelwood School only passed on a 10% increase to parents.
This decision reflects our commitment to support our school community over the long term. We believe this approach is a fair and balanced solution that ensures we can continue to provide the highest standards of education and care whilst acknowledging the financial pressures faced by many of our families.
All published fees are inclusive of VAT and our preferred method of payment is termly direct debit.
Please contact us for further details regarding fees for extra services, such as our bus service, extended day care and any extra academic study support.
School Fees in Advance
Hazelwood offers parents of pupils in Reception upwards (not applicable for Nursery fees) the opportunity to pay fees in advance via our Composition Fees Scheme.
Originally established to allow grandparents to contribute funds and reduce the value of their estate—thereby potentially lessening inheritance tax—the scheme continues to provide financial benefits. Currently, the Composition Scheme offers a 3% discount on prepaid fees.
Details are included below or from our Director of Finance, via [email protected]

The Admissions Process
Choosing a school for your child is a big decision and can feel a little overwhelming, but at Hazelwood we aim to make the process as straightforward as possible. We welcome applications at multiple entry points across our Nursery and Prep School.
Any Questions?
As a co-educational, non-selective school, Hazelwood is committed to treating every applicant equally. We are proud to foster a diverse and inclusive learning environment where high-quality, innovative teaching techniques, supports enriching experiences and positive outcomes for all our pupils.
Please do not hesitate to contact me by phone or email with any queries about the admissions process or to arrange a visit. I'd be delighted to have an informal telephone conversation or meet with you to provide you with a private guided tour of Hazelwood in action.
Kate Whitehead Director of Marketing, Admissions & Communications [email protected] 01883 912037
Steps To Entry
Embark on the journey to join Hazelwood School through our simple seven-step process. From introduction to settling in, we're here to guide you every step of the way.
STEP 1: Introduction
Our website gives you an insight into the aims, values and ethos of the School. Please contact us to enquire whether there is a place available for your child.
STEP 2: Tour
We hold open mornings throughout the year, but you may also wish to get to know us further by booking a private tour, which will allow you to see the school in action and ask any questions you may have.
STEP 3: Registration
Following your visit, if you decide that you would like your child to join Hazelwood School or Nursery, it is necessary to register your child.
Please complete the online registration form and make an online payment of £120 (non-refundable registration fee) for Hazelwood School or £120 (non-refundable registration fee) for Hazelwood Nursery.
Your child will then be added to our admissions list.
STEP 4: Taster Session
Nursery and Reception
The Head of Early Years will seek assurances from parents about their children.
Years 1 to 8
We recommend your child joins us for a taster session. This helps to ensure that starting at Hazelwood is a happy and familiar experience.
STEP 5: Offer
Subject to places being available and on the completion of a satisfactory taster session, we will offer your child a nursery or school place. An offer letter, acceptance form and our Terms and Conditions will be sent to you in advance of the proposed joining date.
Payment of a £500 deposit is required to ensure your child's place, which will be held on your account and refunded when your child leaves Hazelwood.
STEP 6: Class Induction
During the term before joining, your child will be invited to come into Hazelwood to meet their prospective classmates and become familiar with the school environment. For Reception admissions, your child will be invited to a ‘meet the teacher day’ and other settling-in sessions.
STEP 7: First Day of School
Every effort is made to ensure your child’s first day at Hazelwood is enjoyable and relaxed. All members of staff pay particular attention to new starters and a current pupil will be chosen to be their buddy for as long as deemed necessary.
We are so impressed by the journey the school has taken our children on. From the care and excitement that the staff inject into the Early Years, to the extraordinary enrichment provided by the unrivalled Year 7 & 8 programme; we have seen our children blossom into independent teenagers, completely ready for the challenges of secondary school.

School Partnerships
Building strong links and relationships in our community with local schools is something we’re passionate about and keen to develop further.
Opportunities Through Sharing
Schools working together in partnership can be beneficial by uniting pupils and staff through various disciplines and channels: creative and performing arts, sport, supporting wellbeing, teaching practices and shared learning.
At Hazelwood, we believe it is important to share our resources, facilities and knowledge. We work with several local state schools to do this. Such partnerships enable the sharing of best practices and expertise as we work together to support pupil learning opportunities.
Working together can help build stronger schools and better pupil outcomes.​​​
Collaboration with Oxted School
Through shared projects and learning opportunities, we collaborate with Oxted School to enrich educational experiences. Pupils develop real-world skills, confidence and broaden their understanding of future education and career pathways.
Industry Insights Programme
We welcome guests from a wide range of industries into Hazelwood to help pupils discover strengths, develop skills and gain insights that will help shape future choices. By working with industry professionals on real-life problems, pupils step outside the classroom, think differently and develop a deeper understanding of what excites and motivates them. We invite a group of pupils from Oxted School to join us, adding a fresh perspective.
Our pupils attend an annual Careers Fair, kindly hosted by Oxted School.
Workshop Sponsorship
We were delighted to sponsor a legal workshop at Oxted School, where pupils had an interactive courtroom experience to learn about law, rights and responsibilities.
Our Initiatives
Thank you for your help funding this legal workshop. It was amazing, not only did the two groups have fun but they had an insight into a real crime. A fantastic workshop and a great opportunity for the children. You certainly brought the world of work into the hall.
Mr Orozco, Careers Lead, Oxted School
We are looking to create even more opportunities to partner with local schools and share resources, facilities and knowledge. If you are part of a school or educational institution that is interested in a partnership, please get in touch by emailing [email protected]

Upper School Trips
At Hazelwood, our wide range of Upper School trips plays a pivotal role in enriching each pupil’s learning experience, by providing real-world context and fostering independence.
In the upper years, trips become more varied and exciting, with numerous opportunities to participate in residential trips, encouraging social development and the chance to make some wonderful memories.
Residential trips are a great place for pupils to learn to navigate new surroundings, manage their time and collaborate with their peers outside of the familiar classroom setting. These experiences contribute to the development of essential life skills, including problem-solving, adaptability and decision-making.
Exposure to new experiences can spark a pupil’s sense of curiosity, encouraging them to explore subjects beyond the classroom and ultimately broaden their perspective.
At Hazelwood, trips provide a multi-faceted approach to learning, combining academic, social and personal development.

Welcome to Upper School
Welcome to Upper School, where Years 5 to 8 prepare pupils for their next educational chapter through specialised teaching, rigorous academics and comprehensive pastoral care.
Upper School Learning Centre
Our Upper School Learning Centre opened in September 2024 in The Ruth Bourne Building. It has state-of-the art features, such as collaboration zones, brainstorm areas and a wellbeing garden.
This modern and inspiring facility has been specifically designed to meet the needs of our older pupils and provide a hub of creativity and innovation.
With uniquely designed seating, space-saving desks and break-out zones to encourage group discussion and problem solving, our pupils are able to thrive in a dynamic environment, tailored to foster teamwork and academic excellence.
Years 5 & 6
Years 5 and 6 build upon the exceptional foundations that children experience in Years 3 and 4. At this stage, pupils benefit from being taught by specialists across the subject range. The curriculum is broad, blending academic rigour with our innovative and modern approach to teaching. Critical thinking, problem solving and collaborative work are at the heart of everything that the children do in their lessons.
Specialised Curriculum and Preparation
Maths and English are taught in four groups, with the children benefiting from even smaller class sizes to enhance their learning. D&T is introduced in Year 5, while subjects such as Graphics and Latin begin in Year 6. Preparation for senior school entrance exams is an important part of the two-year process as we believe in giving the children the best opportunity to succeed in these tests.
Personalised Support and Guidance
Despite the move away from the traditional primary model at the start of Year 5, the children continue to benefit from first-class pastoral care. The role of the form tutor is vital; children will see their tutor at least once a day, with the focus being on monitoring each child’s academic progress and their wellbeing. The expectations on the pupils are different from Year 4 and while some pupils adapt quickly, others require additional support with areas such as organisation. In addition to the form tutor, the children benefit from having a dedicated Head of Year, alongside the wider pastoral team.
In Years 5 and 6, the children enjoy sports three times per week, alongside PE lessons. A huge array of clubs are available to them and there is a residential trip in both year groups.
Years 7 & 8
In Years 7 and 8, the children enjoy a senior school experience, while remaining in a familiar environment and being at the top of a prep school.
Independence and Empowerment
Pastoral care remains at the forefront of what we do. The children benefit from being in small form groups, allowing them to build an even stronger relationship with their form tutor. At this stage, we introduce vertical tutoring, which allows peer mentoring and the ability to discuss challenging and relevant topics in a safe and controlled manner. Pupil voice is further expanded in Years 7 and 8, offering the children the ability to have a say in how the school is run. In Year 8, every child is afforded responsibility, which further fosters confidence and self-esteem.
Balancing Tradition with Innovation
Children are taught in groups that rarely exceed fifteen, which allows close attention in each individual session; lessons are taught by staff that love working with this age group. Academic rigour is essential and we are guided by our senior schools on the skills that they want to see the children arrive with when they enter Year 9.
In the core subjects, the Common Entrance syllabus is followed and the children have practice exams to ensure that this is a less daunting task when they arrive in their senior school. Equally, our innovative and adaptive approach to education that the children are familiar with does not stop; we firmly believe in equipping the children with the skills that they will require later in life. We continue to encourage the children to read broadly and with ambition.
Exploring Creative Passions and Sporting Talents
Our creative arts provision is comprehensive and pupils are given the opportunity to ‘major’ and “minor” in their preferred subject area, whether that be Graphic Design, D&T, or Art. Similar flexibility is offered within their single games lesson, with a scope of different sporting activities to choose from alongside the major sports. All children are given the chance to participate in school fixtures against a variety of prep and senior schools and many of our children play in tournaments across the year.
Electives
Our Year 7 & 8 Electives Programme on a Friday afternoon allows pupils to choose a topic for half a term that they are passionate about.
We chose Hazelwood Years 7 and 8 for our child because it provided a safe, challenging and inspiring environment for her to grow and mature before the big jump that her senior state education in Year 9 would throw at her. We couldn’t be happier with all she has gained emotionally and academically from her two years at the school.
Former Hazelwood Parent

Our Governors
The Governors would like to welcome you to Hazelwood School.
Governance and Strategic Direction
As well as being a registered charity, Hazelwood is also a company limited by guarantee and is managed by a board of trustees and governors. The object of the School or trust is "the advancement and promotion of education”.
The Head and Deputy Heads (appointees of the Governors) are responsible for the day-to-day management of the School, but it is the Governing Body who is ultimately responsible for the direction which the School takes in the long term i.e. the strategic and development plan, covering such issues as education, property and building development, finance, risk management and resource planning.
Responsibilities and Structure
To ensure that the Governors meet the requirements of the School being an educational charity, the Governing Body is also expected to understand fully, as well as actively monitor such things as health and safety, compliance and safeguarding, public benefit and financial audit. There are also regulatory and legal requirements laid down by the DCSF, OFSTED, IAPS etc. all of which the Governors are charged with responding and reacting to.
Governors serve for an initial term of 3 years, but this is sometimes extended as necessary. The Governing Board has a Secretary and Chair. The full board meets once a term and more recently has met annually away from School to discuss strategy and future development. The Board is subdivided into smaller sub-committees to make the work required more achievable.
